subskill: Quadratic model: equal outputs give the axis, then the maximum
prompt: A company's monthly profit P, in dollars, from selling a product at a price of p dollars is modeled by P(p) = -3p^2 + bp - 400, where b is a constant. According to the model, the company earns the same monthly profit when the price is 6 dollars as when the price is 40 dollars. What is the maximum monthly profit, in dollars, according to the model?
explanation: Because P(6) = P(40), the axis of symmetry of the parabola is halfway between them, at p = (6 + 40)/2 = 23. For P(p) = -3p^2 + bp - 400 the axis is p = b/(2*3) = b/6, so b/6 = 23 and b = 138. The maximum occurs at p = 23: P(23) = -3(529) + 138(23) - 400 = -1587 + 3174 - 400 = 1187.
solve: const a=-3,c=-400; const h=(6+40)/2; const b=-2*a*h; return a*h*h+b*h+c;

distractor_solve.467: const a=-3,c=-400; const h=(40-6)/2; const b=-2*a*h; return a*h*h+b*h+c;
distractor_solve.2774: const a=-3,c=-400; const h=(6+40)/2; const b=-2*a*h; return c - b*b/(2*a);
distractor_solve.5948: const a=-3,c=-400; const h=6+40; const b=-2*a*h; return a*h*h+b*h+c;

mechanism: equal outputs give the axis of symmetry
evaluate at the axis for the maximum
quantity_asked: maximum monthly profit (the value of P at its vertex)

plugback.why: The option is a value of P, not of p or b; to check it a student must first find b from the equal-profit condition and the vertex, which is the whole solution. There is no printed equation an option can be dropped into.

467.why: Takes the axis as half the gap between the prices, (40 - 6)/2 = 17, instead of their midpoint 23, giving b = 102 and P(17) = 467; the stem gives no way to compare this with the answer before solving.

2774.why: Uses the vertex value c - b^2/(2a) instead of c - b^2/(4a); whether this lands above or below depends on the signs of a and c and on b, which is found only by solving.

5948.why: Uses the sum of the two prices, 46, as the axis instead of their average, giving b = 276, and evaluates there; the stem does not show which way this moves the value.

subskill: Horizontal line meeting a parabola: count of levels
prompt: In the xy-plane, the graph of y = -2(x - 3)^2 + 50 is a parabola. A horizontal line y = c, where c is an integer, crosses the parabola at two different points, and both points lie to the right of the y-axis. How many different values of c are possible?
explanation: The parabola opens downward and its highest point is (3, 50). A horizontal line y = c crosses it at two different points exactly when c < 50; the two points are symmetric about the line x = 3, at x = 3 +/- sqrt((50 - c)/2). The right-hand point always has x > 0. The left-hand point has x > 0 when the line lies above the point where the parabola crosses the y-axis: at x = 0, y = -2(9) + 50 = 32, so c must satisfy 32 < c < 50. (At c = 32 the left-hand point is (0, 32), on the y-axis, not to its right.) The integers 33, 34, ..., 49 number 49 - 33 + 1 = 17.
solve: let n=0; for(let c=-500;c<=500;c++){ const d=(50-c)/2; if(d<=0) continue; const r=Math.sqrt(d); const x1=3-r, x2=3+r; if(x1>1e-12 && x2>1e-12) n++; } return n;

distractor_solve.5: const f0=50-2*3; let n=0; for(let c=-500;c<=500;c++){ if(c>f0 && c<50) n++; } return n;
distractor_solve.8: let n=0; for(let c=-500;c<=500;c++){ const d=50-c; if(d<=0) continue; if(3-Math.sqrt(d)>1e-12) n++; } return n;
distractor_solve.49: let n=0; for(let c=-500;c<=500;c++){ if(c>0 && c<50) n++; } return n;

mechanism: two crossings below the top value
both crossings right of the y-axis needs c above the y-intercept
quantity_asked: number of integer values of c for which the line y = c crosses the parabola at two points with positive x-coordinates

plugback.why: The option is a count of values of c, not a value that can be substituted into the equation. To check any count a student must find both bounds (c < 50 and c > 32, the y-intercept), which is the whole solution.

5.why: Computes the y-intercept as 50 - 2(3) = 44, forgetting to square, so counts 45 to 49; the stem does not reveal whether that slip raises or lowers the count until the bound is found.

8.why: Writes the solutions as 3 +/- sqrt(50 - c), dropping the factor 2, so requires 50 - c < 9 and counts 42 to 49; dropping a factor inside the square root can widen or narrow the range, and the stem does not say which.

49.why: Requires the line to lie above the x-axis (c > 0) instead of requiring the crossing points to lie right of the y-axis, and counts c = 1 to 49; the stem gives no way to compare that range with the true one without finding the y-intercept.

structure_check: I slot. The parabola has a highest point, but the asked quantity is a count of levels between two bounds; errors in the lower bound move the count down (5, 8) and misplacing the condition moves it up (49), so the structure does not sign every error.
intermediate_check: 5: no - it is the count from a wrong bound; no printed relation turns 5 into 17. 8: no - a count from a wrong square-root condition; nothing printed converts it to 17. 49: no - the count of positive c below 50; reaching 17 needs the y-intercept 32, which is not printed.
shape_check: The answer is a nonnegative integer: all four survive. Two solutions requires c < 50, so the count is at most the number of integers below 50 that also exceed some lower bound; all four are at most 49. No symmetry or sign property separates the options.
interior_parity_check: Middle values 8 and 17: both plain positive integers, one and two digits (within one); the key 17 is the less clean of the two, so it is not the cleaner one.
arith_class_check: Options 5, 8, 17, 49: three odd and one even (8, a distractor); none of 5, 8, 17 is a multiple of the others' common factor; 49 is a square and 17 is prime - the key is not alone in any class the stem implies.

subskill: Factored product equal to a nonzero constant: other solution
prompt: In the xy-plane, the graph of y = (x - 1)(x - k), where k is a constant, meets the horizontal line y = 40 at two points. One of these points has x-coordinate -4. What is the x-coordinate of the other point?
explanation: The point with x-coordinate -4 is on both graphs, so (-4 - 1)(-4 - k) = 40: (-5)(-4 - k) = 40, -4 - k = -8 and k = 4. The intersection points satisfy (x - 1)(x - 4) = 40. Because the right side is 40, not 0, the answers are NOT 1 and 4 (those are where the graph meets the x-axis). Expand and move 40 to the left: x^2 - 5x + 4 - 40 = 0, so x^2 - 5x - 36 = 0 and (x - 9)(x + 4) = 0. The x-coordinates are -4 and 9, so the other point has x-coordinate 9.
solve: const a=1,m=40,s=-4; const k=s-m/(s-a); const B=-(a+k), C=a*k-m; const d=Math.sqrt(B*B-4*C); const r1=(-B+d)/2, r2=(-B-d)/2; return Math.abs(r1-s)>1e-9?r1:r2;

distractor_solve.4: const a=1,m=40,s=-4; const k=s-m/(s-a); return k;

mechanism: substitute the known solution to find k
move the constant so one side is zero
factor (or use the sum of solutions) for the other solution
quantity_asked: x-coordinate of the second point where y = (x - 1)(x - k) meets y = 40, given that one point has x-coordinate -4

7.why: Takes the sum of the solutions as k - 1 = 3 instead of k + 1 = 5 (a sign slip on the 1 in x - 1), then subtracts the known solution: 3 - (-4) = 7; nothing in the stem shows which way this moves the answer.

-11.why: Uses the product of the solutions as (1)(4) + 40 = 44 instead of 4 - 40 = -36, then divides by the known solution -4. The stem does not reveal how this changes the answer, because the known solution's sign enters the division.

Here the product is divided by the known solution, which is negative (-4), so the over-large product turns into a value BELOW the key. A student can see this only after relating the product to the known solution.

The stem fixes one solution and asks for the other; errors go both ways - treating each factor as equal to 40 gives 41 (above), while taking k as a solution, a sign slip in the sum, or adding 40 into the product give values below - so the structure does not sign every error.

subskill: Value of a quadratic expression at a solution
prompt: Let t be a real number such that 2t^2 - 12t = 30. What does the expression (t - 11)(t + 5) - 3t(t - 6) equal?
explanation: Expand the expression: (t - 11)(t + 5) = t^2 - 6t - 55 and -3t(t - 6) = -3t^2 + 18t. Their sum is -2t^2 + 12t - 55 = -(2t^2 - 12t) - 55. Because 2t^2 - 12t = 30, the value is -30 - 55 = -85. (The solutions t = 3 + sqrt(24) and t = 3 - sqrt(24) both give -85.)
quantity_asked: value of (t - 11)(t + 5) - 3t(t - 6) for a solution t of 2t^2 - 12t = 30

plugback.why: The option is the value of a different expression, not a value of t. The solutions of the equation are irrational (3 +/- sqrt(24)), so a student cannot test an option by putting it into the printed equation; checking any option means expanding and combining the expression, which is the whole solution.

25.why: Takes (-11)(5) as +55, so the value becomes -30 + 55; the effect of a sign slip on one term is not visible from the stem.

-40.why: Evaluates (t - 11)(t + 5) = (t^2 - 6t) - 55 = 15 - 55 and stops, leaving out the -3t(t - 6) part; the stem does not show the sign or size of the omitted part until it is expanded and evaluated.

-36.why: Writes the constant term of (t - 11)(t + 5) as -11 + 5 = -6 instead of (-11)(5) = -55; the stem gives no way to compare -6 with the true constant without expanding.

counter_error.why: Uses t^2 - 6t = 30, forgetting to divide 2t^2 - 12t = 30 by 2, and gets (30 - 55) - 90 = -115, past the key on the low side.

far_distractor.why: Stopping one step early, after evaluating only the first product, ordinarily leaves a value short of the full one. Here the part left out, -3t(t - 6) = -3(t^2 - 6t) = -45, is negative, so stopping early lands ABOVE the key. The sign of that part is known only after it is rewritten in terms of t^2 - 6t and evaluated.

structure_check: No universal condition, extreme value or bound is involved: the expression has one fixed value for either solution. Errors go both ways - forgetting to halve the equation gives -115 (below), while stopping early, mis-forming the constant, or a sign slip give values above - so the structure does not tell a student which way every error goes.
intermediate_check: -40: no - it is the value of (t - 11)(t + 5); getting from -40 to -85 needs -3(t^2 - 6t) = -45, and neither t^2 - 6t = 15 nor 45 is printed. -36: no - a wrong constant; no printed relation turns -36 into -85. 25: no - a sign slip; no printed relation turns 25 into -85. The solved intermediate t^2 - 6t = 15 is not an option.
cheap_bound_check: The cheapest one-sided reading is that the expression is negative (the first product is negative for t between -5 and 11, and the solutions are about -1.9 and 7.9); -40 and -36 sit on the key's side of that bound, so it strikes only 25.
shape_check: The value is the same for both solutions and is an integer (the equation fixes 2t^2 - 12t): all four are integers. A negativity reading keeps -85, -40 and -36. No other property separates them, so at least three options survive every property together.
interior_parity_check: Middle values -40 and -36: both negative two-digit integers of the same form; the key is not interior.
arith_class_check: Parity: -85 and 25 odd, -40 and -36 even, so the key is not alone; signs: three negative, one positive; the key is not alone in sign, integrality, roundness or squareness (25 and -36 are signed squares, -85 and -40 are not).

subskill: Rewriting a quadratic in standard form: coefficients
prompt: When (x + 5)^2 - 4(x + 5) - 26 is multiplied out and like terms are combined, the result is x^2 + bx + c. What is c - b?
explanation: Expand each part: (x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 10x + 25 and -4(x + 5) = -4x - 20. Combining, x^2 + 10x + 25 - 4x - 20 - 26 = x^2 + 6x - 21, so b = 6 and c = -21. Therefore c - b = -21 - 6 = -27.
